newsitem.title: USA: Retail stocks seen having strong 2nd-half '97 - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Retail stocks seen having strong 2nd-half '97 - WSJ.

text.p: Retail stocks may reverse a longstanding trend and have a strong second half of the year in 1997, the Wall Street Journal reported in its 'Heard on the Street' column, citing analysts.

In the paper's electronic edition on Wednesday, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Jeffrey Edelman said retail stocks' relative earnings per share growth in comparison with the market as a whole makes them attractive.
He said he expects Wal-Mart, Nordstrom, May Department Stores, Federated Department Stores, Dayton Hudson, Sears and Kohl's all to see accelerating earnings per share in the double-digits in 1998.
In eight of the past ten years, the S&P retail composite index has had a much weaker second half of the year than first, the paper said.
